Next slice should add more focused upstream gix-merge fixtures, more rename heuristics, broader credential prompt/program invocation semantics, or controlled crate-level upstream runner evidence. The proxy credential lifecycle slice maps helper-returned credentials to store/erase callbacks after successful or failed smart HTTP requests, and the later default requester SOCKS slice covers native SOCKS handshakes. The default PHP requester now implements native SOCKS4/SOCKS4a/SOCKS5/SOCKS5h CONNECT handshakes for smart HTTP receive-pack over HTTP and HTTPS, including TLS peer verification through a configured CA file for HTTPS-over-SOCKS discovery. The latest commit-token iterator slice maps gix-object CommitRefIter token order, SHA-256 token IDs, multi-line extra-header tokens, message tokens, and partial error returns after prior successful tokens. The previous commit-signature slice maps gix-object/gix-actor actor parsing boundaries, including SHA-256 commit IDs, trimmed author/committer accessors, lenient malformed email delimiter handling, complete timestamp consumption, encoding, and multiline gpgsig headers, and now maps commit message summary/title/body parsing, trailer block heuristics, attribution filters, pgp_signature access, and signed-data extraction that removes the signature header bytes. The latest BodyRef commit-message slice maps gix-object MessageRef/BodyRef title-body splitting with LF/CRLF and inconsistent separators, retained title-only trailing newlines, empty bodies, sole-body trailers, folded trailers, exact/below-threshold recognized-prefix footer rules, generic trailer-looking prose rejection, and standalone body trailer parsing for WordPress review notes. The latest annotated-tag slice maps gix-object TagRef parsing for SHA-1/SHA-256 targets, target kind validation, optional taggers, empty/missing separator messages, line-boundary PGP signature detection, and commit mergetag parsing into native tag objects. The latest annotated-tag write slice maps Gitoxide WriteTo semantics for tag body roundtrips, all-newline messages, PGP signature emission, size accounting, and tag name validation, while exposing an ordered token stream for WordPress release provenance. The latest annotated-tag ref-iterator slice preserves raw uppercase object-header bytes separately from normalized object IDs, exposes partial token results before decode errors, and updates the WordPress signed release-tag fixture so provenance hashes roundtrip exact tag bytes. Full raw byte-range token borrowing and broader owned-vs-borrowed tag writer parity remain future work. The latest commit trailer byte-class slice treats vertical tab as upstream whitespace for trailer blank separators, folded trailer continuations, and leading/trailing trailer value trim, while preserving Gitoxide summary-fold behavior that keeps a vertical tab immediately before an internal newline. The latest commit write slice maps gix-object CommitRef::write_to output, size(), and commit object kind by emitting canonical commit storage bytes, object-wrapping them, and exposing WordPress import/deploy commit storage/object hashes. The latest tag-name sanitization slice maps gix-validate byte-level sanitize behavior into GitTag::sanitizeName and adds WordPress draft release-tag normalization before tag construction. The bounded upstream runner evidence is crate-level only: gix-object --lib passed 10 tests, but full workspace and gix-object integration-test parity remain open. The latest reference-name slice maps gix-ref FullNameRef category/short-name helpers, Category::to_full_name construction, namespace expansion/prefix/strip helpers, and a WordPress deployment reference classification fixture for local, remote-tracking, tag, pseudo, main-worktree, linked-worktree, worktree-private, and namespaced refs. The latest reference validation slice maps gix_validate::reference::name complete-name semantics: slash-containing names like `heads/main`/`hello/world` are valid, standalone names must be uppercase pseudo refs, and malformed push/ad advertisement guard tests now reject truly invalid standalone lowercase refs. The latest commit parser slice tightens Commit::parse() to follow gix-object decode::commit header order instead of accepting standard commit headers anywhere in the header block; late parent/encoding names are now exposed as extra headers, matching the upstream parser boundary. The namespaced reference-store iteration slice maps gix-ref store namespace transparency: store iteration and loose iteration strip the namespace, prefix iteration works store-relative, packed refs are filtered through the store namespace, symbolic targets inside the namespace are stripped, and redundant namespaced lookups miss in a namespace-aware store. The latest reference transaction slices map PreviousValue-style update/delete guards, namespace-transparent loose reference writes/deletes, packed-ref delete/update rewrites, default loose shadow updates for packed refs, explicit packed update modes that leave or prune loose source refs, all-packed delete removal of packed-refs, object-update reflog append lines, reflog deletion, peeled-tag object lookup for packed updates, and deref update/delete splitting where symbolic parents become log-only edits, update leaves receive object writes, and delete reflog-only leaves remove parent plus leaf reflogs while preserving both refs. Lock rollback and full filesystem-lock semantics remain unported. The latest TagRef-to-owned slice maps the Gitoxide boundary where borrowed TagRef write_to preserves raw parsed target bytes, TagRef::into_owned parses the target into an ObjectId, and owned Tag write_to emits normalized object IDs after conversion. The WordPress annotated-tag fixture now proves parsed uppercase release-tag targets roundtrip exactly, generated draft release tags use canonical lowercase object IDs, and parsed imported tags can be converted to owned canonical tag bytes through GitTag::toOwned(). The latest smart HTTP followRedirects slice maps Gitoxide HTTP FollowRedirects::Initial/All/None semantics into PHP options: default/initial follows only discovery redirects, false/none rejects redirects, and true/all permits safe same-host receive-pack POST redirects while preserving the generated request body. The latest gix-credentials context slice maps credential helper context encoding/decoding, blank-line termination, quit boolean parsing, URL destructuring, prompt/display URL helpers, and secret redaction/clearing for deployment logs. The latest gix-credentials cascade slice maps helper ordering, partial credential merge and overwrite, failed-helper continuation, helper URL destructuring, expired credential clearing, quit handling, query-user-only bogus password boundaries, and store/erase payload fan-out without invoking git credential.
